question: What is the primary definition of salpingitis?

options.B: Swelling of the ovaries due to cysts
options.C: Infection of the inner uterine lining
options.D: Bacterial colonization of the vaginal canal

explanation: Salpingitis specifically refers to the inflammatory condition affecting the fallopian tubes, often secondary to an ascending infection. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h1)

question: Why do infections easily spread from the fallopian tubes into the pelvic cavity?

options.A: Their thick walls trap bacteria permanently
options.B: Their open ends lead directly into the pelvic cavity
options.C: They connect directly to the bladder
options.D: They lack blood supply to fight germs

explanation: The ends of the fallopian tubes open directly into the pelvis, allowing bacteria to easily pass into surrounding structures. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h1)

question: Which two common bacteria are most often responsible for acute salpingitis?
explanation: These two sexually transmitted organisms cause the vast majority of infectious salpingitis cases worldwide. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h2)

question: How do bacteria usually travel to the fallopian tubes in pelvic infections?

options.A: Upward from the lower genital tract
options.B: Through the bloodstream from skin wounds
options.D: Through lymphatic vessels from the gut

explanation: Infections typically begin in the vagina or cervix and travel upward through the uterus into the fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h2)

question: What long-term structural damage happens inside the fallopian tubes after a severe infection?
explanation: As severe inflammation heals, it leaves behind fibrous scar tissue that can distort and block the inside of the tubes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h3)

question: Why does infected fluid in salpingitis often cause pelvic organs to stick together?

options.A: It causes immediate tissue death in pelvic bones
options.B: It blocks blood flow and melts cells together
options.C: It acts like glue to bind tissues
options.D: It irritates pelvic surfaces and causes sticky scar bands to form

explanation: When infection spills into the pelvis, it irritates the lining of the organs, leading to sticky bands of tissue called adhesions. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h3)

question: What is the main symptom patients report with acute salpingitis?

options.B: Sharp pain in the right shoulder
options.C: Pain in both lower sides of the abdomen

explanation: Inflamed fallopian tubes typically cause tenderness and aching in both lower quadrants of the abdomen. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h4)

question: A patient has lower tummy pain, fever, and abnormal discharge after unprotected sex. What is the most likely condition?
explanation: The combination of pelvic pain, fever, discharge, and risk factors points directly to an upper reproductive tract infection. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h4)

question: During a physical exam, what finding is classically linked to upper reproductive infections like salpingitis?

options.B: Pain when the cervix is moved

explanation: Moving the cervix during an exam stretches the inflamed pelvic tissues, causing sharp pain. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h5)

question: Why is a pelvic ultrasound ordered if a patient is suspected of having severe salpingitis?

options.A: To check the day of the ovulation cycle
options.B: To see individual bacteria under the screen
options.C: To look for abscesses or pockets of infected fluid
options.D: To measure the size of the uterus

explanation: Ultrasound imaging helps identify complications like fluid collections or abscesses that need special medical or surgical care. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h5)

question: Why must antibiotics be started immediately for suspected salpingitis?

options.A: To prevent long-term bladder control issues
options.B: To prevent permanent scarring and infertility

explanation: Early treatment stops the inflammation quickly, lowering the chance of permanent tubal damage and future fertility problems. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h6)

question: Which situation means a patient needs hospital admission and intravenous (IV) antibiotics instead of pills at home?

options.C: Mild lower belly discomfort without fever
options.D: Presence of a suspected pelvic abscess

explanation: Abscesses, high fevers, or failure to improve with oral medications require hospital admission for IV treatment and close monitoring. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h6)

question: Why is a patient with severe salpingitis sometimes placed in a semi-Fowler's (head of bed elevated) position?

options.A: To stop them from rolling over
options.B: To increase blood flow to the womb
options.C: To help infected fluid drain downward into the pelvis
options.D: To prevent acid reflux from drugs

explanation: Elevating the head of the bed uses gravity to keep infected fluid pooled safely in the lower pelvis away from upper organs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h7)

question: A patient asks why her sexual partner must also take medication for salpingitis. What is the best response?

options.A: It stops you from passing the infection back and forth
options.B: Partners always share the same blood type
options.C: It makes your monthly period return faster
options.D: Hospitals require partner treatment for records

explanation: Treating both partners at the same time is necessary to clear the infection and prevent immediate reinfection. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h7)

question: What major reproductive problem is directly linked to tubal scarring from salpingitis?
explanation: Blocked or scarred fallopian tubes make it hard for eggs to travel normally, leading to infertility or dangerous pregnancies outside the womb. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h8)

question: Why does damage to the tiny hair-like cilia inside the fallopian tubes cause infertility?

options.A: The womb lining becomes too thick
options.B: Ovaries stop making eggs due to chemical changes
options.C: Vaginal fluids destroy sperm too quickly
options.D: The tubes cannot push the fertilized egg toward the uterus

explanation: Cilia are tiny hair-like structures that sweep the egg along the tube; losing them stops proper movement toward the womb. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h8)
